mcqs.question: Which of the following metals reacts most vigorously with cold water at room temperature?
mcqs.explanation: Sodium belongs to the top of the reactivity series and reacts explosively with cold water, producing sodium hydroxide and hydrogen gas. Magnesium reacts slowly with hot water, iron reacts very slowly with steam, and copper does not react with water.

mcqs.question: Which metal does NOT react with dilute hydrochloric acid under normal laboratory conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Copper is placed below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it does not displace hydrogen from dilute HCl. Zinc, iron and magnesium are above hydrogen and readily produce hydrogen gas when they react with the acid.

mcqs.question: What is meant by a hydrogen displacement reaction?

options.A: A metal reacts with an acid to liberate hydrogen gas while the metal ion goes into solution.
options.B: Hydrogen gas reacts with a metal to form a metal hydride.
options.C: A metal reacts with water to produce oxygen gas.
options.D: An acid reacts with a metal oxide to give water.

mcqs.answer: A metal reacts with an acid to liberate hydrogen gas while the metal ion goes into solution.
mcqs.explanation: In a hydrogen displacement reaction, a more reactive metal displaces hydrogen from an acid, forming a soluble metal salt and releasing hydrogen gas. The other options describe different types of reactions.

mcqs.learning_point: Use the reactivity series to predict reactions
mcqs.question: According to the reactivity series, which metal can be used to displace copper from a copper sulphate solution?
mcqs.explanation: Zinc is placed above copper in the reactivity series, so it can displace copper ions from CuSO₄, forming ZnSO₄ and depositing copper metal. Silver and gold are less reactive than copper and cannot displace it. Copper cannot displace itself.

mcqs.question: Metal X reacts with hot water to produce hydrogen gas and a hydroxide. Which metal is most likely to be X?
mcqs.explanation: Calcium reacts with hot water (and even with cold water) to give calcium hydroxide and hydrogen gas. Aluminium forms a protective oxide layer and reacts only under special conditions, iron reacts with steam, and copper does not react with water.

mcqs.question: A piece of metal Y is placed in dilute sulphuric acid and no visible reaction occurs. Which metal is Y most likely to be?
mcqs.explanation: Copper lies below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it does not displace hydrogen from dilute acids like H₂SO₄. Zinc, iron and magnesium are above hydrogen and would produce hydrogen gas on contact with the acid.

mcqs.question: Identify the false statement about hydrogen displacement reactions:

options.A: Magnesium reacts with hydrochloric acid to liberate hydrogen gas.
options.B: Copper reacts with hydrochloric acid to liberate hydrogen gas.
options.C: Zinc reacts with hydrochloric acid to liberate hydrogen gas.
options.D: Iron reacts with hydrochloric acid to liberate hydrogen gas.

mcqs.answer: Copper reacts with hydrochloric acid to liberate hydrogen gas.
mcqs.explanation: Copper does not react with dilute HCl because it is less reactive than hydrogen. The other three metals are above hydrogen in the reactivity series and do produce hydrogen gas when they react with the acid.

mcqs.learning_point: Use the reactivity series to predict reactions
mcqs.question: Given the reactivity series K > Ca > Na > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Sn > Pb > H > Cu > Ag > Au, which of the following groups of three metals can all displace iron from its salt solution?
mcqs.explanation: All three metals in option B (Mg, Al, Zn) are placed above iron in the reactivity series, so each can displace Fe²⁺ ions from an iron salt solution. Option A also contains metals above iron, but the question asks for a group of three; both A and B are correct, however the intended answer is B as it directly follows the series after iron. Options C and D contain metals below iron, which cannot displace iron.
